summary: Feed s135_double to SIEM is degraded: 4.2% TCP packet loss exceeds 1% threshold and 76.7% of frames are ERSPAN-encapsulated and not stripped, leaving SIEM with incomplete and unparsable traffic.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN source dropping packets under load - 117 of 2811 TCP packets (4.16%) show gaps/retransmissions, well above 1% threshold. Indicates broker egress buffer exhaustion or oversubscription before the 1Gbps SIEM port, even though tool_overload check is healthy.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives incomplete flows; ~4% of TCP transactions missing, causing missed events, broken correlation and reduced detection/forensic coverage despite SIEM not requiring both directions or full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute feed across multiple broker egress ports or SIEM ingest members to eliminate buffer drops and keep loss <1%.

findings.root_cause: Traffic forwarded via ERSPAN encapsulation (2279 of 2971 frames, 76.7%) and packet broker is not stripping tunnel headers before delivery. Broker is passing outer ERSPAN to tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM sees outer ERSPAN headers instead of inner original IP/TCP; cannot parse or index inner fields, so ~77% of traffic is opaque to SIEM rules and analytics, creating major detection blind spot.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to strip ERSPAN encapsulation and deliver native inner packets so SIEM can parse L3-L7 fields and generate events.
